rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §17 is the deep-module fix and it is already in the plan: the per-run supervisor's behaviour (`_supervisor_command` plus its helpers in the 12,672-line `reckon/crew/dispatch.py`) is to move behind one module whose interface is the spec it reads and the run-directory records it writes, with `supervisor_main.py` kept as the single launch seam.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §18's body names only `fleet_supervisor.state_directory` (which resolves `FLEET_STATE_DIR`) as the owner to extend, and so would retire `dispatch._fleet_record_path`'s `RECKON_FLEET_RECORD` and `XDG_STATE_HOME` overrides rather than move them into the owner; the correction that keeps them lives only in a comment.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §17 creates a new module (an importable public-definition surface) and its body states neither what it retires or merges nor why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the mechanism it extends for every new behaviour it proposes (`_stranded_launch` at `reckon/crew/recovery.py:6613` for §16, `member_in_flight_verdict` at `reckon/crew/node.py:357` for §11, `fleet_supervisor.state_directory` at `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:253` for §18, the seven supervisor helpers in `reckon/crew/dispatch.py` for §17), so no subsystem is added without a searched-for predecessor.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §16's section body adds a release-at-refusal behaviour over machinery that already owns stranded-launch release, and it does not name that owner, so as written it reads as a second release path rather than an extension.
